The test image shows a soybean plant pulled from the ground. Key features:
- Pale/whitish stem
- Collapsed, wilted dark grayish-green leaves
- Root system visible
- Whole plant appears dead/dying

Top candidates: Sudden_death_syndrome, Phytophthora, Brown_Stem_Rot, Charcoal_Rot, White_Mold

Now viewing one reference per candidate class:

I've now used all 8 reference views across 5 classes. Comparing to the test image:

- **Test image**: Plant pulled from ground, pale/bleached white stem, collapsed wilted dark leaves, root system visible
- **White_Mold** (Dise_133): Bleached/pale stem — matches the pale white stem in the test image well
- **White_Mold** (Dise_291): Wilted/collapsed plant — matches overall appearance
- **Phytophthora** references: Show wilting in wet-soil context but brown/tan leaves while standing, less matching
- **Charcoal_Rot**: Field-level yellowing, no pulled-plant context
- **Brown_Stem_Rot**: Cut stem with brown pith — doesn't match
- **SDS**: Interveinal chlorosis pattern on leaves — doesn't match the collapsed whole-plant presentation

The pale/bleached white stem combined with complete plant collapse is most consistent with White Mold (Sclerotinia stem rot).
